newsitem.title: JAPAN: M'bishi Chemical to shut naphtha cracker on May 12.
newsitem.headline: M'bishi Chemical to shut naphtha cracker on May 12.

text.p: Mitsubishi Chemical Corp said on Tuesday it plans to shut its naphtha cracker in Mizushima, western Japan, from May 12 for about a month for routine maintenance.
The plant has annual ethylene output capacity of 450,000 tonnes, a company spokesman said. The plant will resume operations on June 16.

Mitsubishi Chemical, Japan's largest petrochemical firm, also plans to shut another naphtha cracker for about a month from mid-September, he said. That plant, in Yokkaichi, central Japan, has an annual production capacity of 276,000 tonnes.
The exact dates for the turnaround have not been set.
Mitsubishi Chemical's two other naphtha crackers, which are located at its Kashima plant near Tokyo and have a combined output capacity of 720,000 tonnes, will be running through the year, he added.
